official.deadline_note: There is no application deadline for the doctoral study income. The university states that as a full-time doctoral student 'you receive a doctoral study income in a guaranteed minimum amount of 1.2 times the minimum wage in Czechia during the standard length of your studies (4 years)', i.e. it is a standing entitlement attached to full-time enrolment rather than a call.
official.status_note: Standing entitlement: the page is published and describes the guarantee as applying to full-time doctoral students, with no call, round or closing date attached to it.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The page states that most faculties offer 'merit-based scholarships for outstanding students and various forms of tuition fee waivers or reductions' after the first year of studies, with the exact amounts set by each faculty's internal regulations; no tuition waiver is stated for the doctoral study income itself.
benefits: Guaranteed doctoral study income of a minimum of 1.2 times the minimum wage in Czechia during the standard length of doctoral studies (4 years)
The income may consist of a doctoral scholarship, a salary or a wage for creative activities directly related to the preparation of the dissertation, or a combination of both
Often supplemented by awards for participation in research projects and remuneration for teaching undergraduates
eligibility: Enrolled as a full-time doctoral student at Charles University
Within the standard length of the doctoral study programme (4 years)
requirements: Enrol full-time in a doctoral study programme at Charles University

For the separate Václav Havel Bursary: demonstrate that studies are hindered or prevented by repression under totalitarian, authoritarian or other non-democratic regimes; it applies to students of both foundation and degree programmes
For faculty awards: consult the faculty's own scholarship and bursary rules and its Admission Office, because amounts are set by faculty regulations
selection_criteria: The doctoral study income is not competitive; it is described as a guaranteed minimum for every full-time doctoral student
Merit-based scholarships and tuition fee waivers offered by faculties after the first year of studies are competitive and faculty-specific
coverage: Guaranteed minimum doctoral study income during the standard length of studies (4 years)
Often supplemented by awards for participation in research projects and teaching remuneration
application_method: For the doctoral study income: none - it is paid as a guaranteed entitlement to enrolled full-time doctoral students
For the Václav Havel Bursary: apply through the Charles University page for that bursary
For faculty awards: contact the faculty's Admission Office directly
official.application_route: No application is needed for the doctoral study income itself; the competitive awards on the same page are applied for separately through the faculty or the named programme.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the guarantee applies to any full-time doctoral student; the same page directs international applicants to the MEYS scholarships for developing countries and to the International Visegrad Fund scholarships, and to faculty schemes such as MFF, STARS and FSV UK SCHOLARS
official.duration: Standard length of doctoral studies (4 years)
official.description: As a full-time doctoral student you receive a doctoral study income in a guaranteed minimum amount of 1.2 times the minimum wage in Czechia during the standard length of your studies, which may consist of a doctoral scholarship, a salary or wage for creative activities directly related to the preparation of the dissertation, or a combination of both.
official.program_type: Institutional guaranteed doctoral study income (stipend or salary) for full-time doctoral students

applicant_utility.summary: This is an entitlement, not a competition: enrol full-time in a CU doctoral programme and the income floor follows, so your effort goes into the doctoral admission, not into a scholarship application. What is genuinely variable is the form it takes - a doctoral scholarship, a salary or wage for dissertation-related creative work, or a mix - and who pays it, which is decided by your faculty and supervisor. Treat the 1.2x minimum wage figure as a floor, not a target: top-ups from research-project awards and teaching are common and are the part you negotiate.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Candidates admitted full-time to a CU doctoral programme who want a guaranteed income floor while they write up, especially where a supervisor can add project or teaching money on top.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your doctoral programme is full-time, since the guarantee is stated for full-time doctoral students only
Ask your future supervisor and the doctoral studies office how the income is delivered at that faculty - scholarship, wage for dissertation-related work, or a combination
Budget against the floor (1.2x the Czech minimum wage) rather than against any advertised stipend figure, since CU publishes no amount
Separately check the faculty's own post-first-year merit scholarships and tuition fee waivers, whose amounts are set by faculty regulations
If you are affected by repression, check the separate Václav Havel Bursary listed on the same page
common_rejection_risks: Enrolling part-time, which removes the guarantee
Assuming the income covers tuition - it is stated as income, and tuition waivers are a separate faculty-level matter
Waiting for a salary that has been agreed in principle but not contracted through the faculty
Confusing this guarantee with the competitive MEYS, Visegrad or faculty schemes listed on the same page
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, unless your faculty separately grants a waiver, plus anything above the guaranteed minimum - CU publishes no figure, so you must budget against the Czech minimum wage times 1.2 and treat extras as variable.
document_audit: No documents are required for the income itself; documentation starts only at doctoral admission and at faculty level for the separate competitive awards
For the Václav Havel Bursary you must be able to document that studies are hindered or prevented by repression under a non-democratic regime
For faculty awards, the faculty's own rules govern - ask the Admission Office for the current list rather than relying on the university page
alerts: The guarantee runs for the standard length of the doctorate (4 years), not indefinitely
The income is a floor stated in terms of the Czech minimum wage, so it moves with national minimum wage changes rather than with a fixed scholarship table
The competitive faculty scholarships and tuition waivers become available only after the first year of studies
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure full-time doctoral admission at CU, then let the faculty set up the income as scholarship, wage or a combination; no separate scholarship submission is involved for the income itself.
